page: Microsoft Azure M128-64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores, 2 threads per core) operating at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache and hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES cryptography.

A defining characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity of 3892.0 GB, providing approximately 60.81 GB of RAM per core. This is paired with 4194 GB of local storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. There are no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results show a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core/memory performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth (both read and write) are strong, placing in the top 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput consistently register in the average range.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong memory bandwidth, this server is qualitatively positioned as a highly resource-dense option for memory-intensive workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring massive RAM footprints, though it is less optimal for single-threaded compute-bound tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure M128-64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor, it provides 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 3892.0 GB (approximately 60.81 GB per core) and 4194 GB of local storage, with no integrated GPUs. While single-core benchmark performance is relatively weak, falling in the bottom 10%, the instance delivers strong large-block memory read and write bandwidth in the top 25%, alongside average multi-core CPU and database performance. This hardware profile makes the M128-64ms highly cost-efficient for memory-bound applications rather than raw single-threaded compute. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and heavy caching workloads.
